# AuthentID - eMRTD Chip Identity Verification

> Reads the biometric chip in an e-passport and matches the stored portrait against a live face.

Author: Muhammad Tanveer (Full-Stack AI Automation Engineer)
Contact: mtanveertahir66@gmail.com | https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-tanveer-advenno/
Repository: https://github.com/haddindeve/authentid-emrtd-face-verification
Source availability: implementation held in a private repository; access on request.

## Summary
Photo-based identity checks verify that a document looks real, not that it is genuine or that the person presenting it is its holder. A convincing forgery passes; the chip that would expose it goes unread.

Read the eMRTD chip itself, take the portrait the issuing authority stored there, and match it against a live capture. Verification then rests on data signed by the issuer rather than on the printed surface, which is the part a forger controls.

## Stack
Language: Python, Standards: ICAO eMRTD data groups, Biometrics: Face matching pipeline, Security: Certificate validation

## Capabilities
- eMRTD chip data extraction
- Issuer certificate validation
- Portrait-to-live-face matching
- Automated verification test coverage

## Outcomes
- Verification anchored to issuer-signed chip data rather than the printed page
- Document authenticity and holder identity checked in one flow

## FAQ
Q: What is an eMRTD?
A: An electronic machine-readable travel document - a passport or ID card with a chip holding issuer-signed biometric data.

Q: Why read the chip instead of the photo page?
A: The printed page is what a forger controls. The chip is signed by the issuing authority and can be validated.

Q: What does face matching add?
A: It confirms the person presenting the document is the holder recorded on it.

Q: Is the code public?
A: No - private repository, access on request.
